ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
As shown in the figure, a uniform U-shaped tube is placed vertically. The upper end of the left tube is closed, while the upper end of the right tube is open and sufficiently long. Two sections of mercury are used to enclose ideal gases in parts A and B. The height difference between the left and right mercury surfaces at the bottom is $\Delta L{=}6\mathrm{cm}$, and the height of the mercury column above the right tube is $h{=}18\mathrm{cm}$. The initial environmental temperature is $27^{\circ}\mathbf{C}$, the length of gas A is $l_{1}{=}13\mathrm{cm}$, and the external atmospheric pressure is $p_{0}{=}76\mathrm{cmHg}$. Now, while keeping the temperature constant, mercury is slowly injected into the right tube until the left and right mercury surfaces at the bottom are at the same height. Then, the gas in part A is slowly heated to restore the length of the gas column in A to $13\mathrm{cm}$.

1. What is the height $\Delta h$ of the mercury injected into the right tube?
2. What is the temperature of the gas in part $A$ when the length of the air column in $A$ is again $13\mathrm{cm}$?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description first: The figure shows a vertical uniform U-shaped tube. The left branch has a closed upper end and contains gas A above the lower mercury surface. The right branch is open at the top and is sufficiently long; in the right branch there is an upper mercury column open to the atmosphere, gas B below it, and the lower mercury surface. The labeled height of the upper mercury column is h, and the labeled height difference between the right and left lower mercury surfaces is ΔL, with the left lower mercury surface lower than the right one. Reasoning: Take the initial state as state I. Since the upper mercury column in the right tube is open to the atmosphere, the pressure of gas B initially is p_B1 = p0 + h = 76 + 18 = 94 cmHg. Because the left lower mercury surface is ΔL = 6 cm lower than the right lower mercury surface, the pressure of gas A initially is p_A1 = p_B1 + 6 = 100 cmHg. The initial gas-A length is l_A1 = 13 cm and T1 = 27°C = 300 K. Mercury is injected isothermally until the two lower mercury surfaces become level. The lower mercury section has fixed volume in a uniform U-tube, so eliminating the initial 6 cm level difference makes the left lower surface rise 3 cm and the right lower surface fall 3 cm. Thus the length of gas A changes from 13 cm to l_A2 = 10 cm. By Boyle's law for gas A, p_A1 l_A1 = p_A2 l_A2, so p_A2 = 100 × 13 / 10 = 130 cmHg. When the two lower mercury surfaces are level, p_B2 = p_A2 = 130 cmHg. Therefore the required upper mercury column height in the open right tube is p_B2 − p0 = 130 − 76 = 54 cm. Initially it was 18 cm, so the injected mercury height is Δh = 54 − 18 = 36 cm. For the heating step, the upper mercury column length remains 54 cm, so gas B keeps pressure p_B3 = p0 + 54 = 130 cmHg. Heating gas A until its length returns from 10 cm to 13 cm makes the left lower surface move down 3 cm; by fixed lower-mercury volume in the uniform U-tube, the right lower surface moves up 3 cm. Thus the 6 cm level difference is restored, with the left lower surface lower, so p_A3 = p_B3 + 6 = 136 cmHg. For gas A between state II and state III, use pV/T = constant with uniform tube area, so T3 = T2 × (p_A3 l_A3)/(p_A2 l_A2) = 300 × (136 × 13)/(130 × 10) = 408 K.
